extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark dataset designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms. The dataset comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, with 8 tasks: RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict (L-L), and OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, SemanticConflict (V-L). The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models to generate high-quality, diverse data. The benchmark aims to assess LMMs' ability to recognize conflicting commands, which is challenging for language beginners and vulnerable populations.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., & Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2 [cs.AI].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models (LLMs) to generate high-quality, diverse data. The process involves two main loops: the Language Loop and the Visual Loop. Each loop starts from a seed pool and is processed by a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. The Generator creates initial language/vision data, the Decorator introduces self-contradictions, and the Cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. The resulting dataset is refined to extract new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool, enabling rapid expansion of both the seed pool and the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data for the dataset includes programmatically generated text and images, as well as external datasets like ImageNet for SemanticConflict tasks. The AutoCreate framework uses seed inputs to generate diverse instruction forms, complexities, and scopes, which are then processed through the Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner to produce high-quality conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset construction involves deliberate manipulation of data to introduce conflicts. For example, in RuleConflict, a rule is established in the context, and a violating sentence is crafted to challenge the rule. In AttributeConflict, contradictory descriptions are generated for attributes of fictitious objects. In ExclusionConflict, mutually exclusive instructions are paired. In ForbbidenConflict, questions are crafted that inherently require the use of a forbidden word. For vision-language conflicts, images are manipulated to introduce contradictions with textual descriptions, such as altering data in FigureConflict or substituting class names in SemanticConflict.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The AutoCreate framework includes a Cleaner component that removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. The resulting high-quality dataset is refined to extract new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool, ensuring that only high-quality conflicts are included in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset does not involve traditional human annotation for labels, as the conflicts are programmatically generated. However, human experts are involved in quality checking and refining the dataset to ensure high standards. The conflicts are designed to test the ability of LMMs to detect inconsistencies in instructions, rather than to provide labeled responses.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) are used as part of the AutoCreate framework to generate, decorate, and clean the dataset. The framework leverages LLMs to create initial data, introduce contradictions, and ensure quality standards are met.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into three levels: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%) to cater to different needs. The dataset is designed to be expandable, with the AutoCreate framework enabling rapid expansion by refining new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool. The maintainers provide updates and ensure the quality of the dataset through human expert checks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and framework aim to advance the ability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect self-contradictory instructions, which is crucial for improving human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. The proposed Cognitive Awakening Prompting (CaP) approach enhances context-aware understanding, fostering trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may inherit biases from the large language models (LLMs) used in the AutoCreate framework, as the generation of conflicts relies on the outputs of these models. Additionally, the dataset focuses on specific types of conflicts (e.g., rule violations, attribute contradictions), which may not cover all possible forms of self-contradictory instructions. The use of ImageNet for SemanticConflict tasks may also introduce biases related to the dataset's inherent characteristics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, with no fine-grained control over the degree of conflict. The study does not provide a detailed analysis of the attention mechanisms of large multimodal models when confronted with conflicting instructions. Additionally, the dataset may not generalize to other modalities or more complex forms of self-contradictory instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The primary use case of the dataset is to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect self-contradictory instructions. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of LMMs to improve their ability to recognize conflicting commands. The dataset is also useful for researchers and practitioners aiming to enhance the robustness and reliability of AI systems in handling complex, real-world instructions.
